findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime-ordered querysets (breaks the new audit-log path)
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))...)`, i.e. it assumes a numeric sort key, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value unchanged. The only caller added in this PR (organization_auditlogs.py) uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the attribute is a `datetime`. On the very first page, `build_cursor` calls `get_item_key` on the results and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, so any request with `?optimized_pagination=true` against a non-empty audit log returns a 500. Even if the key type were fixed, value_from_cursor would need to convert the millisecond cursor value back to a datetime (as DateTimePaginator does); as written the integer is compared directly against a timestamp column, which Postgres rejects. This paginator is effectively a copy of the numeric Paginator and cannot serve the endpoint it was added for.

findings.title: "Advanced" negative-offset path passes a negative slice to the Django ORM and raises
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when `enable_advanced_features` is on and the client supplies a cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `?cursor=0:-5:0`), the code computes `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then evaluates `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django explicitly disallows negative slicing on querysets and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, so this request 500s. The inline comment ('The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically') is simply wrong. The feature gated behind `enable_advanced_features=True` — which the audit-log endpoint passes unconditionally in its optimized branch — is therefore broken for any negative-offset cursor, legitimate or malicious.

findings.title: organization_context.member.has_global_access crashes when member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every GET to this endpoint, even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested. `organization_context.member` is `None` for requests authenticated without an organization membership (e.g. org auth tokens or API keys carrying org:admin scope), and for any non-superuser such request the attribute access raises AttributeError, turning previously working requests into 500s. Guard for None (e.g. `member = organization_context.member; enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or (member is not None and member.has_global_access)`).

findings.title: Set→sorted-set change will WRONGTYPE-fail on segment keys written before the deploy
findings.body: Segment keys (`span-buf:s:*`) were previously plain Redis sets written with SADD; this PR switches all access to sorted-set commands (ZADD here, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua, ZSCAN in _load_segment_data). Existing keys live up to `redis_ttl` (default 3600s), so after a rolling deploy, any batch or flush touching a pre-deploy key raises `WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value` — the Lua EVALSHA aborts and `p.execute()` raises, failing the whole Kafka batch until those keys expire or are flushed. There is no migration step or type-tolerant handling; this needs an explicit rollout plan (flush the buffer cluster, or drain before enabling).

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now dead configuration; the only enforcement is a hardcoded 1000 in Lua
findings.body: The Python-side guard in `_load_segment_data` that skipped segments exceeding `self.max_segment_spans` (and emitted `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded`) was deleted, but `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans` (default 1001). The only remaining enforcement is the hardcoded `if span_count > 1000` in add-buffer.lua, which neither matches the default (1001) nor any configured value — anyone tuning `max_segment_spans` now gets a silent no-op, and the span-count cap diverges from the documented setting. Either pass the limit into the script as an ARGV or remove the parameter.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default AGGREGATE SUM doubles scores of duplicated spans, skewing eviction
findings.body: `zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` uses Redis's default AGGREGATE SUM, so when the same span payload exists in both source sets (e.g. a duplicate/redelivered span that was previously merged), its score becomes the sum of the two end timestamps — roughly 2× the real time. Since eviction is `zpopmin` (lowest score first), such a duplicated span is artificially protected from eviction and will survive while genuinely newer spans are dropped. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` (or MIN) so duplicated members keep a sane score.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit lowered from 10000 to 1000; over-limit chains silently mis-join segments
findings.body: The redirect resolution loop now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000. When the limit is hit the loop simply ends with `set_span_id` pointing at a mid-chain span, and the incoming span is merged into that mid-chain set (recreating an unlinked key as a new orphan segment) rather than the segment root — fragmenting the segment into separately flushed pieces. Redirect entries persist for `redis_ttl` (1h) for every span id ever seen, independent of the new 1000-span payload cap, so very active traces can still build chains longer than 1000. If the lower bound is intentional, at least log or metric when the loop exits without resolving (redirect_depth == 1000) so the fragmentation is observable.

findings.title: end_timestamp_precise is used as a Redis score without validation; one bad span fails the whole batch
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is passed straight through as the ZADD score for the span payload. `rapidjson.loads` accepts NaN/Infinity, and Redis rejects non-finite ZADD scores with an error, so a single malformed span makes the entire `p.execute()` pipeline fail — failing and reprocessing the whole Kafka batch rather than just the bad span. Previously the payload went into a plain set so this value was never interpreted. Sanitize the score (e.g. skip or clamp non-finite values) before building the ZADD mapping.
